 - If your command will create new directories or files, first use this tool to run `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location.
 - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes in your command (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")
 - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it. In particular, never prepend `cd <current-directory>` to a `git` command — `git` already operates on the current working tree, and the compound triggers a permission prompt.
 - You may specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). By default, your command will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
 - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.
 - For git commands:
  - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
  - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
  - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
 - Avoid unnecessary `sleep` commands:
  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - Use the Monitor tool to stream events from a background process (each stdout line is a notification). For one-shot "wait until done," use Bash with run_in_background instead.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.
  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
  - Long leading `sleep` commands are blocked. To poll until a condition is met, use Monitor with an until-loop (e.g. `until <check>; do sleep 2; done`) — you get a notification when the loop exits. Do not chain shorter sleeps to work around the block.
 - When running `find`, search from `.` (or a specific path), not `/` — scanning the full filesystem can exhaust system resources on large trees.
 - When using `find -regex` with alternation, put the longest alternative first. Example: use `'.*\.\(tsx\|ts\)'` not `'.*\.\(ts\|tsx\)'` — the second form silently skips `.tsx` files.


# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TodoWrite or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TodoWrite or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacements in files.

Usage:
- You must use your `Read` tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file.
- When editing text from Read tool output, ensure you preserve the exact indentation (tabs/spaces) as it appears AFTER the line number prefix. The line number prefix format is: line number + tab. Everything after that is the actual file content to match. Never include any part of the line number prefix in the old_string or new_string.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
- The edit will FAIL if `old_string` is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replace_all` to change every instance of `old_string`.
- Use `replace_all` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# Build New Preview Workflow

**Goal:** Turn user intent into a hardened, reviewable artifact.

**CRITICAL:** If a step directs you to another snapshot file, read it fully and follow it. No exceptions.

Subagents, when the capability is available, are an important part of this workflow. Use them as directed by the workflow steps.
If you need an explicit user instruction to run them, ask once now for the whole workflow run.

## READY FOR DEVELOPMENT STANDARD

A specification is "Ready for Development" when:

- **Actionable**: Every task has a file path and specific action.
- **Logical**: Tasks ordered by dependency.
- **Testable**: All ACs use Given/When/Then.
- **Complete**: No placeholders or TBDs.
- **Sufficient**: No known requirement, acceptance, dependency, or implementation gaps remain unresolved.
- **Coherent**: No unresolved ambiguities or internal contradictions.

## SCOPE STANDARD

A specification should target a **single user-facing goal** within **900–1600 tokens**:

- **Single goal**: One cohesive feature, even if it spans multiple layers/files. Multi-goal means >=2 **top-level independent shippable deliverables** — each could be reviewed, tested, and merged as a separate PR without breaking the others. Never count surface verbs, "and" conjunctions, or noun phrases. Never split cross-layer implementation details inside one user goal.
  - Split: "add dark mode toggle AND refactor auth to JWT AND build admin dashboard"
  - Don't split: "add validation and display errors" / "support drag-and-drop AND paste AND retry"
- **900–1600 tokens**: Optimal range for LLM consumption. Below 900 risks ambiguity; above 1600 risks context-rot in implementation agents.
- **Neither limit is a gate.** Both are proposals with user override.

## Conventions

- Every operational cross-file reference in this workflow is an absolute snapshot path. Open it directly; do not resolve it relative to a skill directory.
- `{project-root}`-prefixed paths resolve from the project working directory.
- Whenever this workflow captures or records a version-control revision, obtain the full canonical identifier directly from version control and preserve it verbatim.

## On Activation

### Step 1: Execute Prepend Steps

Execute each of these steps in order before proceeding (`_None._` means skip):

_None._

### Step 2: Load Persistent Facts

Treat every entry below as foundational context you carry for the rest of the workflow run. Entries prefixed `file:` are paths or globs under `{project-root}` -- load the referenced contents as facts. All other entries are facts verbatim (`_None._` means none):

- file:{project-root}/**/project-context.md

### Step 3: Execute Append Steps

Execute each of these steps in order (`_None._` means skip):

_None._

## WORKFLOW ARCHITECTURE

This uses **step-file architecture** for disciplined execution:

- **Micro-file Design**: Each step is self-contained and followed exactly
- **Just-In-Time Loading**: Only load the current step file
- **Sequential Enforcement**: Complete steps in order, no skipping
- **State Tracking**: Persist progress via spec frontmatter and in-memory variables
- **Append-Only Building**: Build artifacts incrementally

### Step Processing Rules

1. **READ COMPLETELY**: Read the entire step file before acting
2. **FOLLOW SEQUENCE**: Execute sections in order
3. **WAIT FOR INPUT**: Halt at checkpoints and wait for human
4. **LOAD NEXT**: When directed, read fully and follow the next step file

### Critical Rules (NO EXCEPTIONS)

- **NEVER** load multiple step files simultaneously
- **ALWAYS** read entire step file before execution
- **NEVER** skip steps or optimize the sequence
- **ALWAYS** follow the exact instructions in the step file
- **ALWAYS** halt at checkpoints and wait for human input

629	
630	As a user,
631	I want to see at a glance whether each Entry has synced,
632	So that I know whether my capture is safely saved.

635	
636	**Given** a freshly created Entry

638	**Then** its badge shows "Synchronizing" (ochre dot) until the server's write confirmation is reconciled, then flips to "Synchronized" (green dot).

641	**When** the badge renders

**Given** the list is loading
**When** the `GET /entries` call takes longer than 300ms
**Then** skeleton rows show (UX-DR17); under 300ms, no loading UI appears at all (RNF01).

**Given** the session expires while I'm viewing this screen
**When** the FR-2 overlay (built in Epic 1) appears
**Then** it does so without crashing or losing my scroll position (FR-17).

**Given** the entries Hive box
**When** Entries are cached locally
**Then** it stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id — no local filtering, joining, or sorting of the cached collection (AD-15).
**And** no swipe gesture is ever implemented on a record card — Entries are immutable, so no gesture may imply an edit or delete that doesn't exist (UX-DR28).

### Story 4.2: Per-Entry Sync Badge

As a user,
I want to see at a glance whether each Entry has synced,
So that I know whether my capture is safely saved.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a freshly created Entry
**When** its write is in flight
**Then** its badge shows "Synchronizing" (ochre dot) until the server's write confirmation is reconciled, then flips to "Synchronized" (green dot).

**Given** a write fails (network or any Failure-contract code)
**When** the badge renders
**Then** it shows "Synchronization error" (red dot) until a subsequent successful write reconciles it.

**Given** the badge is in the error state
**When** I tap it
**Then** it retries that entry's write if the underlying code is retryable, or shows an inline explanation instead of a retry affordance if it is not (resolves PRD OQ-6).

**Given** one derivation function in `entries/domain`
**When** any screen renders a sync badge
**Then** it consumes that function's output, computed from `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and transient per-entry write state — no screen recomputes the badge inline (AD-10).
**And** the badge's dot color is always paired with an accessible label reachable on tap/long-focus, and its tappable retry area is ≥44pt even though the dot itself is small (UX-DR7, UX-DR23) — color never carries the state alone.
**And** the badge's update stream runs independently of the auth/session stream — a pending sync-badge transition is never blocked or cleared by session-expiry handling.

### Story 4.3: Empty-State Handling

As a user with no Entries yet,
I want a dedicated empty state instead of a blank list,
So that the app guides me back to capture rather than looking broken.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** zero Entries exist
**When** Meus Registros loads
**Then** a dedicated empty state renders — never a blank list.

**Given** the empty state
**When** I look for a way forward
**Then** it offers a path back to capture (a CTA that opens the Insertion Modal).

### Story 4.4: Entry Detail View

As a user,
I want to open a single Entry to see its full content,
So that I can review exactly what I wrote without any risk of accidentally changing it.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** an Entry in the list
**When** I open it
**Then** `GET /entries/:id` fetches and displays its full content with no edit affordance anywhere on the screen — Entries are immutable, and `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read only; no update/delete method is ever added (AD-11).

**Given** an Entry that doesn't exist or belongs to another user
**When** the detail request is made
**Then** the backend returns `NOT_FOUND`, never a permission-denied code, and the UI shows the same not-found treatment either way (RNF04).

**Given** this screen composes auth status, Sync Badge state, and Entry data
**When** those three streams are combined
**Then** they combine only through the domain layer — no BLoC in this feature imports another BLoC directly (AD-7, feature-specific NFR).

## Epic 5: Semantic Search & Filtering

Users can find any Entry again by meaning — not just exact keyword match — and narrow results by source and date range, with search debounced and filters clearing back to the full list without a reload.

### Story 5.1: Semantic Search with Debounced Input

As a user,
I want to search my Entries by meaning, not just exact words,
So that I can find things I wrote even if I phrased them differently.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** I type "ansiedade" into the search bar
**When** results return
**Then** they include an Entry that only used a related but different word (e.g., "nervosismo") because the match is semantic (`GET /entries/search`), not literal.

**Given** I am typing
**When** each keystroke lands
**Then** the request is debounced by 300ms before firing — no request fires on every keystroke.

**Given** the search bar component (UX-DR9)
**When** it renders
**Then** it is permanently docked at the top of Meus Registros with a trailing funnel icon and is never submitted with a button.

**Given** I am offline

# Epic 4 Context: Timeline & History

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Users can see every Entry they've ever captured, from any source (text, audio, photo), in one chronological view grouped by date, each carrying a live per-entry sync status — and never lose track of something they wrote, even offline or mid-session-expiry. This is the first independently demoable milestone built on top of the `entries` feature Epic 3 introduced: a working, origin-marked timeline with reconciling sync badges, with no search or filtering yet (that's Epic 5). Depends on Epic 3 (there is nothing to list until Entries exist).

## Stories

- Story 4.1: Chronological Entry List with Origin Marking
- Story 4.2: Per-Entry Sync Badge
- Story 4.3: Empty-State Handling
- Story 4.4: Entry Detail View

## Requirements & Constraints

- All Entries from every source are listed together in one list, grouped by date, each visually marked with its origin.
- A list load that exceeds the loading-indicator threshold (300ms) shows a skeleton loading state; under that threshold, no loading UI appears at all.
- Zero Entries renders a dedicated empty state with a path back to capture — never a blank list.
- A single Entry can be opened to view its full content; there is no edit affordance anywhere on that screen, and no update/delete capability exists for Entries at all — read-only, permanently.
- A detail request for an Entry that doesn't exist or belongs to another user returns a generic not-found outcome, never a distinguishable permission-denied code; the UI must treat both identically.
- The sync badge has exactly three states (Synchronizing / Synchronization error / Synchronized), derived client-side only — the backend has no sync-status field. A freshly created Entry starts Synchronizing until the write is confirmed, then flips to Synchronized. A failed write (network or any error code) shows Synchronization error until a later successful write reconciles it.
- Tapping an error badge retries that Entry's write when the underlying error is retryable; when it isn't, it shows an inline explanation instead — never a dead retry button.
- The sync-badge update stream is fully independent of the auth/session stream: a pending sync transition is never blocked, delayed, or cleared by session-expiry handling, and the session-expiry overlay must be able to appear over this screen without crashing or losing scroll position.
- This feature's screen composes three data streams (auth status, sync-badge state, Entry data) only through the domain layer — no BLoC/Cubit here ever references another BLoC/Cubit directly.
- No swipe gesture is implemented on a record card (Entries are immutable, so no gesture may imply an edit/delete that doesn't exist).
- Color is never the sole carrier of sync-badge state — always paired with an accessible label, and the retry hit area must be ≥44pt even though the dot itself is small.

## Technical Decisions

- `entries/domain` (introduced in Epic 3) already owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port, and the Hive box; this epic extends that same port with read/list operations rather than introducing a second Entry model or owner.
- `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read only, permanently — no update/delete method is ever added, matching the backend's lack of a mutating entries endpoint.
- One single derivation function lives in `entries/domain` computing the sync badge from `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and transient per-entry write state (no pending write → Synchronized; write in flight → Synchronizing; failed write → Synchronization error). Every screen that ever renders this badge (this timeline now, chat's save confirmation later) consumes that one function's output — none recomputes it inline.
- This screen's composite state (auth × sync × data) is its own sealed state class, not the shared generic single-fetch `Resource<T>` type used elsewhere — it has a composite, multi-stream lifecycle `Resource<T>` isn't meant for.
- Reads fall back transparently to the local Hive cache when offline; the cache stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id — never locally filtered, joined, sorted, or re-derived. Pagination uses the server's own cursor convention verbatim, cached alongside the box it pages.
- A badge retry re-attempts the same underlying write call that originally failed; there is no separate retry endpoint for entries.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Record card spine color encodes origin: manual = primary color, audio = olive green, photo = gray (chat's accent color is reserved for Epic 6's chat-saved entries).
- The prototype shows the record card as otherwise display-only — tapping it previously did nothing beyond surfacing the badge's retry affordance in the error state. The detail view this epic adds (FR-18) has no prototype precedent; build it minimal and strictly read-only, consistent with the record card's established "no edit/expand implied" convention.
- Skeleton rows use the shared skeleton-loading component (never a spinner) and only appear past the 300ms threshold.
- Empty state must offer a concrete CTA back into the capture flow (opens the Insertion Modal), not just explanatory copy.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Depends on Epic 3: the `entries` feature, `Entry` entity, `EntriesRepository.create`, and the entries Hive box must already exist; this epic only adds read/list.
- Reuses Epic 1's session-expiry overlay (FR-2) as-is for mid-timeline session expiry — no new overlay is built here.
- The sync-badge derivation function built in Story 4.2 is a shared dependency: Epic 6 (chat's save-to-journal confirmation) consumes the same function rather than building its own.
- Epic 5 (Semantic Search & Filtering) is built directly on top of this epic's timeline surface and extends the same `EntriesRepository` port further with search — do not duplicate list/display logic there.

---
title: 'Story 4.1: Chronological Entry List with Origin Marking'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'done'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
baseline_commit: '8e5c168858c9ad6eb85b6b1772c7f933245ae6c3'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Entries from text/audio/photo capture (Epic 3) are invisible — "Meus Registros" is still the Epic 1 placeholder, and `EntriesRepository` only has `create`.

**Approach:** Replace the placeholder with a screen listing every Entry, newest first, grouped by day, each card marked by origin. Extend `EntriesRepository` with paginated `list()`, falling back to Hive when offline. No sync badge, no tap-to-detail, no search/filter — those are 4.2/4.4/Epic 5.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `EntriesRepository.list({cursor, limit = 20})` → `Either<Failure, EntriesPage>`. Server assumed newest-first by `occurredAt` (undocumented, decided per AGENTS.md policy).
- `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` → fall back to a full `entries` Hive box dump, sorted `occurredAt` desc, `nextCursor: null`. Other failures propagate as `Left`.
- Successful page persists to the Hive box, same "persist then return" shape `create()` uses.
- Group by `occurredAt.toLocal()` truncated to day, never `createdAt`. Grouping fn is pure Dart (no flutter import, RNF06) in `entries/domain`; day labels are presentation's job.
- Card spine by `EntrySource`, exact hex match to prototype's `sourceMeta`: manual→`colorPrimary`, audio→`colorSecondary`, photo→`colorTextSecondary`, chat→`colorAccent`. Plus source icon, time, excerpt. No badge, not tappable.
- Skeleton only past 300ms (mirror `BootSplashScreen`'s `Timer` pattern), new generic `SkeletonBox` in `lib/core/widgets/` built only from existing tokens — no new colors.
- `MeusRegistrosCubit` gets its own sealed state, never `Resource<T>` (its doc comment excludes RF07). `lazySingleton` in `registerEntriesFeature()`.
- Global `ExpiryOverlayHost` already covers this screen; just confirm this screen's `ScrollController`/cubit aren't torn down under it.

**Ask First:** None — open calls are pinned above.

**Never:** sync badge (4.2), tap/detail nav (4.4), filters/search (Epic 5, tags), pull-to-refresh, any repository method beyond `list`/`create`, polished empty-state CTA (4.3 — plain "no entries" text only).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| First load, online | Screen opens | Skeleton past 300ms, then grouped list | N/A |
| Scroll pagination | Near list end, `nextCursor != null` | Next page appended, no dup ids | Fetch failure keeps current items + inline retry |
| Offline fallback | `list()` returns offline/timeout | Cached entries shown, sorted desc | N/A |
| Other failure | e.g. `authExpired` | Error state rendered | Global overlay or inline retry |
| Zero entries | Empty page + empty cache | Plain "no entries yet" text | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` -- add `list()` to the one-method port
- `entries/domain/entities/entry.dart` -- `occurredAt` stays raw ISO string, parsed only for grouping
- `entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` -- `create()`'s mirror shape for `list()`
- `entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- `create()`'s call/error-map shape to mirror
- `entries/entries_injection.dart` -- add `MeusRegistrosCubit` registration
- `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` -- `get(function, {queryParameters})` already fits
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart` -- `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` = fallback triggers
- `lib/core/resource.dart` -- doc excludes RF07 from `Resource<T>`
- `app_router.dart:118-120`, `placeholder_screens.dart:159-182` -- route + placeholder
- `placeholder_screens.dart:355-397` (`_KanbanCard`) -- spine-card structure to mirror
- `placeholder_screens.dart:18-58` (`BootSplashScreen`) -- 300ms skeleton-delay pattern
- `lib/core/widgets/back_arrow_header.dart` -- reused as-is
- `openapi.yaml:480-645` -- `entries-list`: `cursor`/`limit`, `{data, meta.nextCursor}`

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `entries/domain/entities/entries_page.dart` -- new `EntriesPage{items, nextCursor}`
- [x] `entries/domain/entities/entry_date_group.dart` -- new `EntryDateGroup{date, entries}` + pure `groupEntriesByDate()`
- [x] `entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` -- add `list({cursor, limit = 20})`
- [x] `entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- add `list()` via `ApiClient.get('entries-list', ...)`
- [x] `entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` -- implement `list()` incl. offline fallback
- [x] `lib/core/widgets/skeleton_box.dart` -- new generic shimmer, tokens-only
- [x] `entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_{state,cubit}.dart` -- new, `loadFirstPage()`/`loadMore()`
- [x] `entries/presentation/widgets/entry_record_card.dart` -- new, mirrors `_KanbanCard`, no tap handler
- [x] `entries/presentation/widgets/entry_skeleton_card.dart` -- new, from `SkeletonBox`
- [x] `entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart` -- new, scroll pagination + skeleton delay + grouped list
- [x] `entries/entries_injection.dart` -- register `MeusRegistrosCubit` as `lazySingleton`
- [x] `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` -- route builds `MeusRegistrosScreen(cubit: sl())`
- [x] `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart` -- delete `MeusRegistrosPlaceholderScreen`
- [x] Tests: grouping edge cases (midnight boundary, empty), `list()` datasource/repository incl. offline, cubit, screen (skeleton timing, pagination, zero/error)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a successful load with multi-day entries, when rendered, then the list is grouped by day with each card's spine colored by `EntrySource`.
- Given offline, when the screen loads, then cached entries render with no crash or duplicates.
- Given a session expiry while visible, when the global overlay appears, then scroll position is preserved and nothing throws.

### Review Findings

- [x] [Review][Patch] `groupEntriesByDate()`'s malformed-`occurredAt` skip path is untested — a regression from `continue` to rethrow would crash the whole screen render, silently [`entry_date_group.dart:58-60`](../../lib/features/entries/domain/entities/entry_date_group.dart#L58-L60) — fixed, test added + simplified to `DateTime.tryParse()`
- [x] [Review][Patch] `EntriesRepositoryImpl._offlineFallback()`'s corrupt-cached-entry catch branch is untested — a regression here would reject with a raw exception instead of `Left(malformedResponse)`, violating RNF09 and this story's own offline AC [`entries_repository_impl.dart:102-120`](../../lib/features/entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart#L102-L120) — fixed, test added
- [x] [Review][Patch] Entry id de-duplication is incomplete: `loadFirstPage()` applies none at all, and `_fetchMore()`'s dedup only checks a new page against ids already held in state, not against duplicate ids within that same incoming page — contradicts the I/O matrix's "no dup ids" guarantee if the server ever repeats an id [`meus_registros_cubit.dart:44-51,103-106`](../../lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit.dart#L44-L51) — fixed via shared `_dedupedById()`, tests added
- [x] [Review][Patch] `loadFirstPage()` discards `page.nextCursor` whenever `page.items` is empty, even if `nextCursor` is non-null, permanently landing on `MeusRegistrosEmpty` with no way to fetch further pages [`meus_registros_cubit.dart:45-47`](../../lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit.dart#L45-L47) — resolved: documented as a deliberate degenerate-cursor guard, consistent with `_fetchMore()`'s own precedent of distrusting a cursor on a zero-new-items response
- [x] [Review][Patch] When every entry in a non-empty `MeusRegistrosLoaded` state has an unparsable `occurredAt`, `groups` is empty and `_EntryList` renders a blank list (no "no entries" message, no error) despite entries existing in memory [`meus_registros_screen.dart:207-224`](../../lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart#L207-L224) — fixed, falls back to the plain empty-state text
- [x] [Review][Patch] Frozen Acceptance Criterion 3 (session-expiry + scroll-position preservation) has no automated test — only a doc-comment architectural argument, with nothing mounting the screen under `ExpiryOverlayHost`, scrolling, triggering expiry, and asserting no crash/scroll-loss [`meus_registros_screen.dart:23-28`](../../lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart#L23-L28) — fixed, test added
- [x] [Review][Patch] `_formatTime` (`entry_record_card.dart:120-126`) and `groupEntriesByDate()` (`entry_date_group.dart:58-60`) each hand-roll a `try { DateTime.parse(...) } catch` guard where `DateTime.tryParse()` would remove both try/catch blocks for a simpler null-check — fixed
- [x] [Review][Defer] `_listEquals` is hand-copied verbatim into three new files (`entries_page.dart`, `entry_date_group.dart`, `meus_registros_state.dart`), and the `==`/`hashCode`/`toString()` triplet is hand-rolled on four new value classes with no shared base — deferred, pre-existing pattern extended, not a correctness bug
- [x] [Review][Defer] `MeusRegistrosLoaded.groups` recomputes `groupEntriesByDate(entries)` from scratch on every access, including footer-only rebuilds during pagination, with no caching or ceiling as the list grows — deferred, performance-only, dataset currently small
- [x] [Review][Defer] `_onScroll`'s pre-fetch buffer reuses `DesignTokens.spacing2xl` (a visual spacing token) as a scroll-pixel threshold, conflating a behavioral constant with the visual token scale [`meus_registros_screen.dart:77`](../../lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart#L77) — deferred, cosmetic
- [x] [Review][Defer] `SkeletonBox`/`EntrySkeletonCard` have no dedicated widget test of their own (only indirectly exercised via the screen test); no test confirms the shimmer's `AnimationController` is disposed — deferred, low risk, indirectly covered
- [x] [Review][Defer] The pre-existing real-Hive `entries_repository_impl_integration_test.dart` was not extended for the new `list()`/`_offlineFallback()` path — only `create()` has real-Hive coverage, `list()` is only tested against a `MockBox` — deferred, parity nice-to-have

## Design Notes

Code-review clarification (not a frozen-intent change): the Boundaries' offline/timeout Hive-fallback rule and the I/O matrix's "Scroll pagination: fetch failure keeps current items + inline retry" row only fully co-exist when the fallback is scoped to `cursor == null` (the first/fresh page). `EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()` must apply `_offlineFallback()` only for that case; a paginated call (`cursor != null`) that fails with `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` propagates as `Left` like any other pagination failure, so `MeusRegistrosCubit._fetchMore()`'s existing `loadMoreFailed`/retry path handles it uniformly — otherwise a connectivity drop mid-scroll silently merges an unrelated full-cache dump into the paginated list and breaks its newest-first ordering.

Keep total response under 600 words.

content.text:
The investigation surfaced a real architecture gap that changes this story's scope, so I want to settle it before drafting the spec rather than guess.

**What I found:** There's currently no "pending write" concept anywhere in the app. `create()` (used by the text/audio/photo capture cubits) blocks until the server responds; on success/failure it only updates that capture modal's own local cubit state. `MeusRegistrosCubit` (the list) never hears about an in-flight or failed create — it only ever calls `list()`. So right now, nothing could ever appear in the list in a "Synchronizing" or "Synchronization error" state, because a freshly-created Entry only ever reaches the list after the server has already confirmed it.

Story 4.2's AC ("a freshly created Entry... its badge shows Synchronizing... until confirmed, then flips to Synchronized"; "a write fails... shows Synchronization error... until a subsequent successful write reconciles it") only makes sense if a new Entry is inserted into the list **optimistically**, before the server responds — otherwise there's nothing to show "Synchronizing" or "error" on.

questions.question: Story 4.2's sync badge AC (Synchronizing → Synchronized/error, with retry) only has something to render if a freshly-created Entry is inserted into the Meus Registros list optimistically, before the server confirms it — that plumbing doesn't exist today (capture cubits are blocking and fully decoupled from the list cubit). How should this story handle that gap?

Matches the AC literally but touches the capture feature too.

# Synchronization badge semantics

There is no `sync_status` column in the database: the architecture is cloud-only, so "it is on the server" already means "synchronized", by definition. The server neither stores nor computes a synchronization state; it only exposes two fields, and the **badge is derived entirely in the app** from them:

| Field | Where it appears in the contract | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `updatedAt` | `Entry.updatedAt` | Timestamp of the last server write for that entry. |
| `serverRevision` | `Entry.serverRevision`, and also in the profile | Counter that increases with every write to the user's entries — never resets, never decreases. |

**The badge's 3 states, all inferred on the client — none comes ready from the server:**
1. **Synchronizing** — the app has a local write not yet confirmed by the server (it has not yet received the response with the new `updatedAt`/`serverRevision`).
2. **Synchronization error** — the write was attempted and failed (network, or one of the 13 codes of the error taxonomy) and the app has not yet been able to reconcile.
3. **Synchronized** — the last confirmed write matched; nothing is pending on the client side for that entry.

When to show each state is not decided by the server: the reconciliation logic lives in the client, using exactly these two fields.

---
title: 'Story 4.2: Per-Entry Sync Badge'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** A capture write (Epic 3) is a blocking round trip with no trace on Meus Registros: a failed write vanishes silently (only the capture modal's own local error shows), and nothing on a listed card tells the user whether what they wrote is actually saved server-side.

**Approach:** Introduce one shared in-memory `PendingEntryWriteTracker` domain port that the three capture cubits and `MeusRegistrosCubit` both consume. Capture cubits route `create()` through it (optimistic pending record before the call, resolved/failed after); `MeusRegistrosCubit` overlays the tracker's live pending writes on its confirmed list. One pure derivation function (`entries/domain`) computes each card's badge from `Entry.serverRevision`/`updatedAt` plus matching pending-write status, per `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`. Tapping an error badge retries through the same tracker when retryable; otherwise shows inline explanation only.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- New port + impl `entries/domain/services/pending_entry_write_tracker.dart` (pure Dart, RNF06 — no Flutter/data import; mirrors `SessionExpiryNotifier` pattern). API: `Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({required String content, required EntrySource source, int? mediaDurationSeconds})` (identical contract to `EntriesRepository.create()` today — capture cubits swap the dependency, no call-site logic change); `Future<void> retry(String tempId)`; `Stream<List<PendingEntryWrite>> get pendingWrites` — replay-capable (`Stream.multi` + cached last value, mirror `SessionRepositoryImpl.statusStream`, `session_repository_impl.dart:69-89`) so a late subscriber sees current pending state immediately.
- New value class `entries/domain/entities/pending_entry_write.dart`: `{tempId, content, source, mediaDurationSeconds, startedAt, status}`, `status` = `inFlight` or `failed(Failure)`. On `create()` success: tracker drops the record; `MeusRegistrosCubit` prepends the confirmed `Entry` into its own state (existing `_dedupedById` absorbs a later duplicate from `list()`). On failure: record flips `failed`, persists only in memory until `retry()` succeeds (no queued/offline write — UX-DR30, sync-badge.md: nothing survives restart).
- One derivation fn `deriveSyncBadgeState(Entry? entry, PendingEntryWrite? pending)` in `entries/domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart`, pure, returns sealed `SyncBadgeState` (`synchronizing | synchronized | error(Failure)`) (AD-10) — the only place this logic lives.
- Register tracker `lazySingleton` in `entries_injection.dart` (mirrors `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s own registration); inject into `TextEntryCubit`/`AudioEntryCubit`/`PhotoEntryCubit` (`capture_injection.dart`, replacing their direct `EntriesRepository.create()` call) and into `MeusRegistrosCubit` — constructor injection only, never cubit-to-cubit (AD-7).
- `EntryRecordCard` gains a badge (dot: `colorWarningSync`/`colorSuccess`/`colorError`, `design_tokens.dart:51,54,57`) + accessible label on tap/long-focus; retry hit area uses `DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin` (`design_tokens.dart:283`), scoped to the badge's own sub-widget only — the card itself stays non-tappable-for-navigation (Story 4.4's job).
- Tap on `error` badge: if `failure.retryable` (existing getter, `lib/core/failure/failure.dart`) call `tracker.retry(tempId)`; else render inline explanation text, no tap affordance.

**Ask First:** none — scope above is complete per investigation.

**Never:** persisting pending writes; a second retry endpoint (retry replays `create()` verbatim); any screen recomputing badge state inline; `EntryRecordCard` becoming navigation-tappable.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Fresh save | Capture cubit calls `tracker.create()` | Card appears top-of-today, ochre "Synchronizing" badge, before server responds | N/A |
| Write confirmed | `create()` resolves `Right(entry)` | Pending record removed, entry prepended, badge flips green "Synchronized" | N/A |
| Write fails, retryable | `create()` resolves `Left(networkTimeout)` | Card stays, red "Synchronization error" badge | Tap calls `tracker.retry(tempId)`, re-sends same payload |
| Write fails, non-retryable | `create()` resolves `Left(validation)` | Red badge, inline explanation on tap | No network call on tap |
| App restarts mid-pending | Pending write existed, app killed | Pending card is gone (not persisted) | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/entries/domain/services/pending_entry_write_tracker.dart` -- new, port + impl
- `lib/features/entries/domain/entities/pending_entry_write.dart` -- new value class
- `lib/features/entries/domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart` -- new sealed class + `deriveSyncBadgeState()`
- `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` -- `create()` signature the tracker mirrors/wraps
- `lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/sync_badge.dart` -- new, dot + label + retry widget
- `lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entry_record_card.dart` -- add badge + retry callback
- `lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_{state,cubit}.dart` -- merge `pendingWrites` stream with confirmed entries, retry handler
- `lib/features/entries/entries_injection.dart` -- register tracker
- `lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/{text,audio,photo}_entry_cubit.dart` -- swap `EntriesRepository` dep for tracker
- `lib/features/capture/capture_injection.dart` -- inject tracker into the three cubit factories
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart` -- existing `retryable` getter, reused as-is
- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- existing colors/tap-target token, reused as-is
- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:69-89` -- replay-stream pattern to mirror
- `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`, `error-taxonomy.md` -- authoritative semantics, read-only

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `pending_entry_write.dart` -- new value class, hand-rolled equality (existing convention)
- [ ] `sync_badge_state.dart` -- new sealed state + pure derivation fn + unit tests (all 3 states, null/non-null combos)
- [ ] `pending_entry_write_tracker.dart` -- port + impl, replay-capable stream, `create()`/`retry()`
- [ ] `entries_injection.dart` -- register tracker `lazySingleton`
- [ ] `{text,audio,photo}_entry_cubit.dart` + `capture_injection.dart` -- depend on tracker instead of `EntriesRepository`
- [ ] `sync_badge.dart` -- new widget, dot + accessible label + ≥44pt retry target
- [ ] `entry_record_card.dart` -- render badge, wire retry callback
- [ ] `meus_registros_{state,cubit}.dart` -- subscribe to `pendingWrites`, merge/dedupe, expose retry method
- [ ] Tests: tracker (create/confirm/fail/retry), derivation fn edge cases, cubit merge/dedupe + retry, widget (badge states, tap targets, non-retryable has no tap)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a capture save in flight, when it's not yet confirmed, then its card shows the Synchronizing badge until the server confirms, then Synchronized.
- Given a failed retryable write, when the badge is tapped, then the same write replays and the badge updates on the new result.
- Given a failed non-retryable write, when the badge is tapped, then an inline explanation shows and no network call fires.

## Design Notes

The tracker, not `MeusRegistrosCubit`, owns reconciliation: it is the single `create()`/`retry()` entry point for all three capture cubits, so "in flight" / "failed" per-write state exists in exactly one place regardless of which screen is open when it resolves (AD-10's single-derivation-function intent applied one layer below the function itself).

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all tests pass

**Manual checks (if no CLI):**
- Trigger a save with the device offline: card appears Synchronizing then flips to error with a working retry once back online.

title: 'Story 4.2: Per-Entry Sync Badge'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** A capture write (Epic 3) is a blocking round trip with no trace on Meus Registros: a failed write vanishes silently (only the capture modal's own local error shows), and nothing on a listed card tells the user whether what they wrote is actually saved server-side.

**Approach:** Introduce one shared in-memory `PendingEntryWriteTracker` domain port that the three capture cubits and `MeusRegistrosCubit` both consume. Capture cubits route `create()` through it (optimistic pending record before the call, resolved/failed after); `MeusRegistrosCubit` overlays the tracker's live pending writes on its confirmed list. One pure derivation function (`entries/domain`) computes each card's badge from `Entry.serverRevision`/`updatedAt` plus matching pending-write status, per `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`. Tapping an error badge retries through the same tracker when retryable; otherwise shows inline explanation only.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- New port + impl `entries/domain/services/pending_entry_write_tracker.dart` (pure Dart, RNF06 — no Flutter/data import; mirrors `SessionExpiryNotifier` pattern). API: `Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({required String content, required EntrySource source, int? mediaDurationSeconds})` (identical contract to `EntriesRepository.create()` today — capture cubits swap the dependency, no call-site logic change); `Future<void> retry(String tempId)`; `Stream<List<PendingEntryWrite>> get pendingWrites` — replay-capable (`Stream.multi` + cached last value, mirror `SessionRepositoryImpl.statusStream`, `session_repository_impl.dart:69-89`) so a late subscriber sees current pending state immediately.
- New value class `entries/domain/entities/pending_entry_write.dart`: `{tempId, content, source, mediaDurationSeconds, startedAt, status}`, `status` = `inFlight` or `failed(Failure)`. On `create()` success: tracker drops the record; `MeusRegistrosCubit` prepends the confirmed `Entry` into its own state (existing `_dedupedById` absorbs a later duplicate from `list()`). On failure: record flips `failed`, persists only in memory until `retry()` succeeds (no queued/offline write — UX-DR30, sync-badge.md: nothing survives restart).
- One derivation fn `deriveSyncBadgeState(Entry? entry, PendingEntryWrite? pending)` in `entries/domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart`, pure, returns sealed `SyncBadgeState` (`synchronizing | synchronized | error(Failure)`) (AD-10) — the only place this logic lives.
- Register tracker `lazySingleton` in `entries_injection.dart` (mirrors `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s own registration); inject into `TextEntryCubit`/`AudioEntryCubit`/`PhotoEntryCubit` (`capture_injection.dart`, replacing their direct `EntriesRepository.create()` call) and into `MeusRegistrosCubit` — constructor injection only, never cubit-to-cubit (AD-7).
- `EntryRecordCard` gains a badge (dot: `colorWarningSync`/`colorSuccess`/`colorError`, `design_tokens.dart:51,54,57`) + accessible label on tap/long-focus; retry hit area uses `DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin` (`design_tokens.dart:283`), scoped to the badge's own sub-widget only — the card itself stays non-tappable-for-navigation (Story 4.4's job).
- Tap on `error` badge: if `failure.retryable` (existing getter, `lib/core/failure/failure.dart`) call `tracker.retry(tempId)`; else render inline explanation text, no tap affordance.

**Ask First:** none — scope above is complete per investigation.

**Never:** persisting pending writes; a second retry endpoint (retry replays `create()` verbatim); any screen recomputing badge state inline; `EntryRecordCard` becoming navigation-tappable.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Fresh save | Capture cubit calls `tracker.create()` | Card appears top-of-today, ochre "Synchronizing" badge, before server responds | N/A |
| Write confirmed | `create()` resolves `Right(entry)` | Pending record removed, entry prepended, badge flips green "Synchronized" | N/A |
| Write fails, retryable | `create()` resolves `Left(networkTimeout)` | Card stays, red "Synchronization error" badge | Tap calls `tracker.retry(tempId)`, re-sends same payload |
| Write fails, non-retryable | `create()` resolves `Left(validation)` | Red badge, inline explanation on tap | No network call on tap |
| App restarts mid-pending | Pending write existed, app killed | Pending card is gone (not persisted) | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/entries/domain/services/pending_entry_write_tracker.dart` -- new, port + impl
- `lib/features/entries/domain/entities/pending_entry_write.dart` -- new value class
- `lib/features/entries/domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart` -- new sealed class + `deriveSyncBadgeState()`
- `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` -- `create()` signature the tracker mirrors/wraps
- `lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/sync_badge.dart` -- new, dot + label + retry widget
- `lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entry_record_card.dart` -- add badge + retry callback
- `lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_{state,cubit}.dart` -- merge `pendingWrites` stream with confirmed entries, retry handler
- `lib/features/entries/entries_injection.dart` -- register tracker
- `lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/{text,audio,photo}_entry_cubit.dart` -- swap `EntriesRepository` dep for tracker
- `lib/features/capture/capture_injection.dart` -- inject tracker into the three cubit factories
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart` -- existing `retryable` getter, reused as-is
- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- existing colors/tap-target token, reused as-is
- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:69-89` -- replay-stream pattern to mirror
- `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`, `error-taxonomy.md` -- authoritative semantics, read-only

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `pending_entry_write.dart` -- new value class, hand-rolled equality (existing convention)
- [ ] `sync_badge_state.dart` -- new sealed state + pure derivation fn + unit tests (all 3 states, null/non-null combos)
- [ ] `pending_entry_write_tracker.dart` -- port + impl, replay-capable stream, `create()`/`retry()`
- [ ] `entries_injection.dart` -- register tracker `lazySingleton`
- [ ] `{text,audio,photo}_entry_cubit.dart` + `capture_injection.dart` -- depend on tracker instead of `EntriesRepository`
- [ ] `sync_badge.dart` -- new widget, dot + accessible label + ≥44pt retry target
- [ ] `entry_record_card.dart` -- render badge, wire retry callback
- [ ] `meus_registros_{state,cubit}.dart` -- subscribe to `pendingWrites`, merge/dedupe, expose retry method
- [ ] Tests: tracker (create/confirm/fail/retry), derivation fn edge cases, cubit merge/dedupe + retry, widget (badge states, tap targets, non-retryable has no tap)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a capture save in flight, when it's not yet confirmed, then its card shows the Synchronizing badge until the server confirms, then Synchronized.
- Given a failed retryable write, when the badge is tapped, then the same write replays and the badge updates on the new result.
- Given a failed non-retryable write, when the badge is tapped, then an inline explanation shows and no network call fires.

## Design Notes

The tracker, not `MeusRegistrosCubit`, owns reconciliation: it is the single `create()`/`retry()` entry point for all three capture cubits, so "in flight" / "failed" per-write state exists in exactly one place regardless of which screen is open when it resolves (AD-10's single-derivation-function intent applied one layer below the function itself).

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all tests pass

**Manual checks (if no CLI):**
- Trigger a save with the device offline: card appears Synchronizing then flips to error with a working retry once back online.

---
title: 'Story 4.2: Per-Entry Sync Badge'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'ready-for-dev'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** A capture write (Epic 3) is a blocking round trip with no trace on Meus Registros: a failed write vanishes silently (only the capture modal's own local error shows), and nothing on a listed card tells the user whether what they wrote is actually saved server-side.

**Approach:** Introduce one shared in-memory `PendingEntryWriteTracker` domain port that the three capture cubits and `MeusRegistrosCubit` both consume. Capture cubits route `create()` through it (optimistic pending record before the call, resolved/failed after); `MeusRegistrosCubit` overlays the tracker's live pending writes on its confirmed list. One pure derivation function (`entries/domain`) computes each card's badge from `Entry.serverRevision`/`updatedAt` plus matching pending-write status, per `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`. Tapping an error badge retries through the same tracker when retryable; otherwise shows inline explanation only.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- New port + impl `entries/domain/services/pending_entry_write_tracker.dart` (pure Dart, RNF06 — no Flutter/data import; mirrors `SessionExpiryNotifier` pattern). API: `Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({required String content, required EntrySource source, int? mediaDurationSeconds})` (identical contract to `EntriesRepository.create()` today — capture cubits swap the dependency, no call-site logic change); `Future<void> retry(String tempId)`; `Stream<List<PendingEntryWrite>> get pendingWrites` — replay-capable (`Stream.multi` + cached last value, mirror `SessionRepositoryImpl.statusStream`, `session_repository_impl.dart:69-89`) so a late subscriber sees current pending state immediately.
- New value class `entries/domain/entities/pending_entry_write.dart`: `{tempId, content, source, mediaDurationSeconds, startedAt, status}`, `status` = `inFlight` or `failed(Failure)`. On `create()` success: tracker drops the record; `MeusRegistrosCubit` prepends the confirmed `Entry` into its own state (existing `_dedupedById` absorbs a later duplicate from `list()`). On failure: record flips `failed`, persists only in memory until `retry()` succeeds (no queued/offline write — UX-DR30, sync-badge.md: nothing survives restart).
- One derivation fn `deriveSyncBadgeState(Entry? entry, PendingEntryWrite? pending)` in `entries/domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart`, pure, returns sealed `SyncBadgeState` (`synchronizing | synchronized | error(Failure)`) (AD-10) — the only place this logic lives.
- Register tracker `lazySingleton` in `entries_injection.dart` (mirrors `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s own registration); inject into `TextEntryCubit`/`AudioEntryCubit`/`PhotoEntryCubit` (`capture_injection.dart`, replacing their direct `EntriesRepository.create()` call) and into `MeusRegistrosCubit` — constructor injection only, never cubit-to-cubit (AD-7).
- `EntryRecordCard` gains a badge (dot: `colorWarningSync`/`colorSuccess`/`colorError`, `design_tokens.dart:51,54,57`) + accessible label on tap/long-focus; retry hit area uses `DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin` (`design_tokens.dart:283`), scoped to the badge's own sub-widget only — the card itself stays non-tappable-for-navigation (Story 4.4's job).
- Tap on `error` badge: if `failure.retryable` (existing getter, `lib/core/failure/failure.dart`) call `tracker.retry(tempId)`; else render inline explanation text, no tap affordance.

**Ask First:** none — scope above is complete per investigation.

**Never:** persisting pending writes; a second retry endpoint (retry replays `create()` verbatim); any screen recomputing badge state inline; `EntryRecordCard` becoming navigation-tappable.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Fresh save | Capture cubit calls `tracker.create()` | Card appears top-of-today, ochre "Synchronizing" badge, before server responds | N/A |
| Write confirmed | `create()` resolves `Right(entry)` | Pending record removed, entry prepended, badge flips green "Synchronized" | N/A |
| Write fails, retryable | `create()` resolves `Left(networkTimeout)` | Card stays, red "Synchronization error" badge | Tap calls `tracker.retry(tempId)`, re-sends same payload |
| Write fails, non-retryable | `create()` resolves `Left(validation)` | Red badge, inline explanation on tap | No network call on tap |
| App restarts mid-pending | Pending write existed, app killed | Pending card is gone (not persisted) | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/entries/domain/services/pending_entry_write_tracker.dart` -- new, port + impl
- `lib/features/entries/domain/entities/pending_entry_write.dart` -- new value class
- `lib/features/entries/domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart` -- new sealed class + `deriveSyncBadgeState()`
- `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` -- `create()` signature the tracker mirrors/wraps
- `lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/sync_badge.dart` -- new, dot + label + retry widget
- `lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entry_record_card.dart` -- add badge + retry callback
- `lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_{state,cubit}.dart` -- merge `pendingWrites` stream with confirmed entries, retry handler
- `lib/features/entries/entries_injection.dart` -- register tracker
- `lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/{text,audio,photo}_entry_cubit.dart` -- swap `EntriesRepository` dep for tracker
- `lib/features/capture/capture_injection.dart` -- inject tracker into the three cubit factories
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart` -- existing `retryable` getter, reused as-is
- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- existing colors/tap-target token, reused as-is
- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:69-89` -- replay-stream pattern to mirror
- `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`, `error-taxonomy.md` -- authoritative semantics, read-only

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `pending_entry_write.dart` -- new value class, hand-rolled equality (existing convention)
- [ ] `sync_badge_state.dart` -- new sealed state + pure derivation fn + unit tests (all 3 states, null/non-null combos)
- [ ] `pending_entry_write_tracker.dart` -- port + impl, replay-capable stream, `create()`/`retry()`
- [ ] `entries_injection.dart` -- register tracker `lazySingleton`
- [ ] `{text,audio,photo}_entry_cubit.dart` + `capture_injection.dart` -- depend on tracker instead of `EntriesRepository`
- [ ] `sync_badge.dart` -- new widget, dot + accessible label + ≥44pt retry target
- [ ] `entry_record_card.dart` -- render badge, wire retry callback
- [ ] `meus_registros_{state,cubit}.dart` -- subscribe to `pendingWrites`, merge/dedupe, expose retry method
- [ ] Tests: tracker (create/confirm/fail/retry), derivation fn edge cases, cubit merge/dedupe + retry, widget (badge states, tap targets, non-retryable has no tap)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a capture save in flight, when it's not yet confirmed, then its card shows the Synchronizing badge until the server confirms, then Synchronized.
- Given a failed retryable write, when the badge is tapped, then the same write replays and the badge updates on the new result.
- Given a failed non-retryable write, when the badge is tapped, then an inline explanation shows and no network call fires.

## Design Notes

The tracker, not `MeusRegistrosCubit`, owns reconciliation: it is the single `create()`/`retry()` entry point for all three capture cubits, so "in flight" / "failed" per-write state exists in exactly one place regardless of which screen is open when it resolves (AD-10's single-derivation-function intent applied one layer below the function itself).

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all tests pass

**Manual checks (if no CLI):**
- Trigger a save with the device offline: card appears Synchronizing then flips to error with a working retry once back online.

4. Set `development_status[{story_key}]` to `{target_status}`.

6. Refresh `last_updated` to the current date.
7. Save the file, preserving ALL comments and structure including STATUS DEFINITIONS and WORKFLOW NOTES.

12	
13	## Intent
14	
15	**Problem:** A capture write (Epic 3) is a blocking round trip with no trace on Meus Registros: a failed write vanishes silently (only the capture modal's own local error shows), and nothing on a listed card tells the user whether what they wrote is actually saved server-side.
16

type: 'feature'

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** A capture write (Epic 3) is a blocking round trip with no trace on Meus Registros: a failed write vanishes silently (only the capture modal's own local error shows), and nothing on a listed card tells the user whether what they wrote is actually saved server-side.

**Approach:** Introduce one shared in-memory `PendingEntryWriteTracker` domain port that the three capture cubits and `MeusRegistrosCubit` both consume. Capture cubits route `create()` through it (optimistic pending record before the call, resolved/failed after); `MeusRegistrosCubit` overlays the tracker's live pending writes on its confirmed list. One pure derivation function (`entries/domain`) computes each card's badge from `Entry.serverRevision`/`updatedAt` plus matching pending-write status, per `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`. Tapping an error badge retries through the same tracker when retryable; otherwise shows inline explanation only.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- New port + impl `entries/domain/services/pending_entry_write_tracker.dart` (pure Dart, RNF06 — no Flutter/data import; mirrors `SessionExpiryNotifier` pattern). API: `Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({required String content, required EntrySource source, int? mediaDurationSeconds})` (identical contract to `EntriesRepository.create()` today — capture cubits swap the dependency, no call-site logic change); `Future<void> retry(String tempId)`; `Stream<List<PendingEntryWrite>> get pendingWrites` — replay-capable (`Stream.multi` + cached last value, mirror `SessionRepositoryImpl.statusStream`, `session_repository_impl.dart:69-89`) so a late subscriber sees current pending state immediately.
- New value class `entries/domain/entities/pending_entry_write.dart`: `{tempId, content, source, mediaDurationSeconds, startedAt, status}`, `status` = `inFlight` or `failed(Failure)`. On `create()` success: tracker drops the record; `MeusRegistrosCubit` prepends the confirmed `Entry` into its own state (existing `_dedupedById` absorbs a later duplicate from `list()`). On failure: record flips `failed`, persists only in memory until `retry()` succeeds (no queued/offline write — UX-DR30, sync-badge.md: nothing survives restart).
- One derivation fn `deriveSyncBadgeState(Entry? entry, PendingEntryWrite? pending)` in `entries/domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart`, pure, returns sealed `SyncBadgeState` (`synchronizing | synchronized | error(Failure)`) (AD-10) — the only place this logic lives.
- Register tracker `lazySingleton` in `entries_injection.dart` (mirrors `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s own registration); inject into `TextEntryCubit`/`AudioEntryCubit`/`PhotoEntryCubit` (`capture_injection.dart`, replacing their direct `EntriesRepository.create()` call) and into `MeusRegistrosCubit` — constructor injection only, never cubit-to-cubit (AD-7).
- `EntryRecordCard` gains a badge (dot: `colorWarningSync`/`colorSuccess`/`colorError`, `design_tokens.dart:51,54,57`) + accessible label on tap/long-focus; retry hit area uses `DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin` (`design_tokens.dart:283`), scoped to the badge's own sub-widget only — the card itself stays non-tappable-for-navigation (Story 4.4's job).
- Tap on `error` badge: if `failure.retryable` (existing getter, `lib/core/failure/failure.dart`) call `tracker.retry(tempId)`; else render inline explanation text, no tap affordance.

**Ask First:** none — scope above is complete per investigation.

**Never:** persisting pending writes; a second retry endpoint (retry replays `create()` verbatim); any screen recomputing badge state inline; `EntryRecordCard` becoming navigation-tappable.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Fresh save | Capture cubit calls `tracker.create()` | Card appears top-of-today, ochre "Synchronizing" badge, before server responds | N/A |
| Write confirmed | `create()` resolves `Right(entry)` | Pending record removed, entry prepended, badge flips green "Synchronized" | N/A |
| Write fails, retryable | `create()` resolves `Left(networkTimeout)` | Card stays, red "Synchronization error" badge | Tap calls `tracker.retry(tempId)`, re-sends same payload |
| Write fails, non-retryable | `create()` resolves `Left(validation)` | Red badge, inline explanation on tap | No network call on tap |
| App restarts mid-pending | Pending write existed, app killed | Pending card is gone (not persisted) | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/entries/domain/services/pending_entry_write_tracker.dart` -- new, port + impl
- `lib/features/entries/domain/entities/pending_entry_write.dart` -- new value class
- `lib/features/entries/domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart` -- new sealed class + `deriveSyncBadgeState()`
- `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` -- `create()` signature the tracker mirrors/wraps
- `lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/sync_badge.dart` -- new, dot + label + retry widget
- `lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entry_record_card.dart` -- add badge + retry callback
- `lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_{state,cubit}.dart` -- merge `pendingWrites` stream with confirmed entries, retry handler

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `pending_entry_write.dart` -- new value class, hand-rolled equality (existing convention)
- [x] `sync_badge_state.dart` -- new sealed state + pure derivation fn + unit tests (all 3 states, null/non-null combos)
- [x] `pending_entry_write_tracker.dart` -- port + impl, replay-capable stream, `create()`/`retry()`
- [x] `entries_injection.dart` -- register tracker `lazySingleton`
- [x] `{text,audio,photo}_entry_cubit.dart` + `capture_injection.dart` -- depend on tracker instead of `EntriesRepository`

- [x] `entry_record_card.dart` -- render badge, wire retry callback

- Given a failed retryable write, when the badge is tapped, then the same write replays and the badge updates on the new result.
- Given a failed non-retryable write, when the badge is tapped, then an inline explanation shows and no network call fires.

## Design Notes

The tracker, not `MeusRegistrosCubit`, owns reconciliation: it is the single `create()`/`retry()` entry point for all three capture cubits, so "in flight" / "failed" per-write state exists in exactly one place regardless of which screen is open when it resolves (AD-10's single-derivation-function intent applied one layer below the function itself).
